title: Expansion microscopy of mouse brain organotypic slice cultures to study protein distribution
protocol: Culture the OTCs for three weeks to ensure maturation and stabilization.
Fix the OTCs using a short fixation method.
Block non-specific binding sites with an appropriate blocking solution.
Incubate the OTCs with the primary antibody overnight at 4°C.
Day 2: Wash, permeabilization, and secondary antibody incubation
Wash the OTCs thoroughly to remove unbound antibodies.
Permeabilize the OTCs to allow deep penetration of antibodies.
Incubate the OTCs with the secondary antibody overnight at 4°C.
Prepare the fixative (4% PFA/1× PBS) fresh.
Store the fixative at 4°C until use.
Prepare the blocking buffer (3% normal donkey serum + 3% normal goat serum in 1× PBST) fresh.
Store the blocking buffer at 4°C until use.
Rinse OTCs briefly in 1× PBS to remove IM completely.
Fix OTCs on ice for 5 min using 1 mL of 4% PFA between the well and the insert, and add a few drops on top of the OTCs.
Wash OTCs 5 × 10 min in 1× PBS on a rocker at 22°C.
Gently scrape OTCs off the insert with two thin spatulas after 2–3 washes.
Transfer scraped OTCs to a 24-well plate.
Incubate OTCs with blocking buffer for 2 h at 22°C on a rocker (250 μL/well).
Incubate OTCs with the primary antibody in blocking buffer at the appropriate concentration for 7 days at 4°C on a rocker (250 μL/well).
Evaluate the quality and specificity of primary antibodies carefully due to stringent permeabilization conditions.
Adjust staining protocol for each antibody as necessary by increasing antibody concentration or enhancing fluorescence proteins.
Include a sample without primary antibody in experiments to evaluate non-specific signals from the sample or secondary antibody.
Wash plate 3 times with 1× PBS (1 ml/well) at 22°C on a rocker for 5 minutes each.
Incubate with secondary antibody in blocking buffer at appropriate concentration for 3 days at 4°C in darkness, wrapped in parafilm to avoid evaporation.
Wash plate 3 times with 1× PBS (1 ml/well) at room temperature for 5 minutes each.
Optional: Counterstain with DAPI at this step.
Incubate the sample in DAPI (1 μg/mL) for 30 min at 22°C using 250 μL/well.
Wash the sample three times for 5 minutes each in 1× PBS.
Optimize imaging parameters according to the imaging setup.
Assess the quality of the staining before proceeding with expansion microscopy.
Measure the distance between two landmarks in the tissue before expansion.
Use readily identifiable pyramidal neurons as landmarks for measurement.
Ensure there is enough PBS to accommodate the working distance of water immersion objectives.
Carefully add fresh PBS directly to the OTC if needed.
Keep OTCs in 1× PBS (1 mL/well).
Wrap the plate in parafilm and aluminum foil.
Store the wrapped plate at 4°C until use.
Proceed with imaging and/or expansion microscopy within a few days after fixation.
Cross-link proteins with a polymer-based gel for expansion microscopy.
Digest tissue, leaving only the anchored proteins within the gel.
Expand the tissue by osmosis in multiple water baths.
Protect all steps from light during staining.
Thaw one Acryloyl-X SE/DMSO aliquot in the fridge.
Dilute the thawed Acryloyl-X SE/DMSO in 1× PBS (for 5 samples: use 10 μL in 990 μL PBS; for 10 samples: use 20 μL in 1980 μL PBS).
Transfer each OTC into the microwell of a MatTek dish.
Add 200 μL Acryloyl-X SE to each microwell containing an OTC.
Wash each microwell twice with 1× PBS for 15 minutes each.
Add 200 μL fresh gelling solution to each microwell and incubate at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Replace the old gelling solution in each microwell with 150 μL of fresh gelling solution.
Carefully place a coverslip on top of each microwell containing the gel and incubate at 37°C for 2 hours.
Gently pull off the coverslip from each microwell (if it adheres, remove both the coverslip and the gel together).
Add 2 mL digestion buffer to each microwell and allow the gel to digest overnight at 22°C.
Add approximately 5 mL distilled or MilliQ water to the dish.
Let the OTC sit for about 20 minutes.
Repeat the process until expansion reaches a plateau (typically after 5–6 baths).
Add viscous agarose around the sample.
Wait a few minutes for the agarose to gel.
Add extra drops of agarose to the edges of the gel to prevent movement in Z.
Ensure OTCs are submerged in the solution to anchor proteins properly.
Thaw the digestion buffer and components for the gelling solution in the fridge.
Wash the OTCs 2 × 15 min in 1× PBS.
Prepare the gelling solution (200 μL/slice) immediately before use as it solidifies fast.
Remove the PBS and carefully add the gelling solution on top of the sample within the microwell.
Incubate in the dark for 30 min at 4°C.
Prepare fresh gelling solution (150 μL/slice) immediately before use.
Carefully aspirate the old gelling solution from the microwell and replace it with freshly prepared solution.
Using forceps, carefully place a 15 μm coverslip on top of the microwell.
Ensure the formation of a flat, smooth gel with a thickness equal to the depth of the microwell.
Incubate for 2 hours in the dark at 37°C.
Carefully peel off the coverslip using straight forceps and check if the gel is completely polymerized.
Prepare a master mix of digestion buffer and proteinase K (2 mL and 20 μL per sample, respectively).
Add 2 mL of the master mix immediately on top of each gel.
Incubate overnight in the dark at 22°C.
Remove the digestion buffer and coverslip on day 3.
Add approximately 5 mL of distilled water per dish when the gel starts to expand and detach from the coverslip.
Renew the water bath with fresh distilled water after about 20 minutes.
Continue adding fresh distilled water until sample size does not increase anymore, indicating maximal expansion has been reached.
Store samples at 22°C in the dark.
Melt 2% agarose in distilled water in the microwave during wash 3 or 4.
Set the water bath to 35°C and keep the agarose in it to prevent solidification.
Remove the agarose from the water bath when it cools sufficiently.
Transfer the sample to be imaged into a 3 cm Petri dish after removing excess water.
Assess the alignment of the OTC in the gel under the epifluorescence lamp.
Ensure the sample is mounted in the correct orientation on top of the gel for upright microscopes.
Use confocal lasers to assess the orientation of the sample within the gel along the Z-axis.
Add agarose around the sample using a cut 1 ml tip once alignment and gelling are confirmed.
Cover the entire dish with agarose to prevent horizontal movement of the sample.
Place drops on the edges of the sample when the agarose is nearly solidified to prevent vertical movement.
Transfer the covered sample with distilled water onto the microscope for imaging.
Use a water immersion objective for high magnification images.
Reimage the Z-stack encompassing the whole stretch with a step size of 0.5 μm.
Use a frame averaging of 3 during reimaging.
Imaging should be performed using two lasers simultaneously at 488 nm (for GFP) and 561 nm (for GluA2 labeled with Alexa 568).
Do not cover the sample itself with agarose as this will cause diffraction.
Perform imaging as soon as possible to avoid laser-induced water loss from the gel.
If necessary, remove the agarose and remount the gel with fresh agarose after 30–45 minutes.
Discard the water after imaging.
Remove the agarose carefully after discarding the water.
Return the sample to the original dish after removing the agarose.
Store the sample in PBS for long-term storage if needed.
